idiom_name: JPA/Hibernate entity hierarchy with Kotlin entity classes (kotlin-jpa / kotlin-allopen plugins)
implementation_notes: Kotlin uses the same JPA metadata as Java - @Inheritance/@DiscriminatorColumn on an open class hierarchy, with the provider generating the mapper structure and resolving polymorphism - but two language properties must be accommodated: entity classes and their mapped members are final unless opened (use explicit open or the kotlin-allopen/kotlin-spring plugin), and JPA needs a no-argument constructor, which the kotlin-jpa (no-arg) compiler plugin synthesises for @Entity/@MappedSuperclass classes. With both plugins the generated mapper behaves exactly as in Java; Exposed, JetBrains' SQL framework, has no inheritance mapping, so there the hierarchy is mapped per table by hand.
pitfalls: Without the kotlin-jpa plugin the provider cannot instantiate entities: no no-arg constructor exists and final classes cannot be proxied.
Data classes are a trap for entities - generated equals/hashCode/toString walk mutable state and break identity maps and lazy proxies.
Mapped properties without defaults break reflective materialisation; give every persisted property a default value.
